marks.gloss_en: כדרב יהודה אמר רב: כל העולם כולו ניזון בשביל חנינא בני, וחנינא בני די לו בקב חרובין -- merit that feeds the world while its owner lacks
כי מהניא זכותייהו -- אעלמא, אדידהו -- לא (= p_zchut_leolam_lo_ledidhu)
when their merit avails, it avails the world, not themselves
והא אמר רבי חייא בר אבא אמר רבי יוחנן: ראה רבי דבריו של רבי שמעון בכסוי הדם -- Rebbi follows R' Shimon on covering the blood (kind svara: no objection kind for והאמר)
(entertained) and if you say [Rebbi] holds an unfit slaughter is called slaughter [and obligates covering]
ומי נפל ליה יאניבא בכיתניה? והאמר רבין בר אבא ... ולא לקה פשתנם, ונתנו חכמים עיניהם ברבי חייא ובניו (kind svara: no objection kind for והאמר)
from when the exiles came up, meteors, earthquakes, storm winds and thunder ceased, their wine did not sour and their flax was not stricken; and the Sages set their eyes on R' Chiyya and his sons
a deaf-mute, an imbecile or a minor who slaughtered while others watch them -- [one is] obligated to cover [the blood]
and likewise for 'it and its offspring': if they slaughtered while others watch them -- it is forbidden to slaughter [the offspring] after them
דתנן: תינוק שנמצא בצד העיסה... ואמרינן: מאי טעמא דרבי מאיר? ... סמוך מיעוטא לחזקה -- the dough mishna shows R' Meir joins a minority to a presumption (no SupportKind names דתנן)
a child found beside the dough with dough in his hand -- R' Meir declares [the dough] pure
סיפא נמי: since the Sages say it is forbidden to slaughter after them, people will say it is a proper slaughter and come to eat from their slaughter!
סיפא, אמרי: בישרא דלא קא מיבעיא ליה -- in the last clause people will say: [he leaves the offspring because] he does not need the meat
רישא נמי, אמרי: לנקר חצירו הוא צריך -- the first clause too: people will say he [covers because he] needs to clean his courtyard (the previous answer's logic, turned against the account)
שחט באשפה, מאי איכא למימר? בא לימלך, מאי איכא למימר? -- if he slaughtered on a garbage heap, what is there to say? if he came to consult, what is there to say?
וליטעמיך, סיפא נמי, בא לימלך -- מאי איכא למימר? -- by your reasoning, the last clause too: if he came to consult, what is there to say? (unanswered; the stam abandons the account at 86a.14)
the premise of the stam's question: the Sages do not dispute the first clause (covering), only the last (it and its offspring)
in the first clause, if we said they are obligated to cover, people would say it is a proper slaughter and come to eat from their slaughter
rather, the Sages dispute the whole matter, and they waited for R' Meir until he finished the matter, and then disputed him
granted the Sages: [they rule] to stringency
R' Meir would obligate [one who eats] from their slaughter on account of [eating] a carcass
for R' Meir is concerned for the minority
